newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian share index unmoved by heavy trade.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian share index unmoved by heavy trade.

text.p: Heavy trade on the Nigerian stock exchange left the index barely changed on Monday as oil shares rose, but some banks lost out, dealers said.
The all-share index closed at 6,524.00 from 6,524.01 on Friday.
Traders said interest in oil shares remained strong, despite relatively high prices, because of generous dividend policies.
Texaco rose 50 kobo to 26.50 naira. Mobil, National Oil and Unipetrol all closed 30 kobo higher at 38.60 naira, 32.50 naira and 40.50 naira, respectively.
Nestle Foods gained 40 kobo to 31.40 naira on a good half-year performance.
Benue Cement continued its rise to close up 25 kobo at 6.25 naira. Ashaka Cement was 20 kobo up at 17.50 naira.

Trading was mixed in the banking sector. Guaranty Trust Bank was 12 kobo higher at 13.62 naira, while Trade Bank closed at 1.77 naira, up five kobo. But market forces saw the shares of three big banks drop.
Union Bank fell four kobo to 8.00 naira, FSB International Bank fell 10 kobo to 4.90 naira and NAL Merchant Bank closed at 5.15 naira, down five kobo.
Packaging companies Carnaud Metal Box and Avon Crowncaps were both down 10 naira at 4.30 naira and 3.90 naira, respectively. Dunlop slid 10 kobo to 11.80 naira.
Conglomerate John Holt fell three kobo to 11.20 naira.
Guinness ended five kobo lower at 8.60 naira, but Nigerian Breweries, in which Dutch brewer Heineken has just increased its stake ended unchanged at 12.28 naira.

Trading resumed in the shares of Nigerian Bottling Co, suspended last week for failing to seek regulators' approval before beginning a merger. The Coke bottlers have now formally applied for permission to conclude a merger with a company currently bottling its brands in eastern Nigeria.
The shares will trade at 28.72 naira -- the price at which it was suspended last Wednesday until the conclusion of the merger. ($1=80 naira)
